items.mathematical_context_and_resolution: In the spectral sequence of a decreasing filtration, B_r is the image of ∂:T^{p+q−1}(F^{p−r+1}/F^p)→T^{p+q}(F^p/F^{p+1}), while Z_r is the image of T^{p+q}(F^p/F^{p+r})→T^{p+q}(F^p/F^{p+1}). For a strict projective system the boundary expression is constant for n≥p and the lifting expression for n≥p+r−1. The d2 statements on printed p.247 are consistent with these corrected conventions and must NOT be interchanged.

items.mathematical_context_and_resolution: The assumptions already give continuous representations V,W and hence a continuous tensor representation V⊗W, so no extra finite-monodromy hypothesis should be added. However VI1.2.5 Remark (EN8741) explicitly distinguishes locally constant from twisted constant: on normal connected X the former requires finite monodromy. Taking X=Spec(F_q), F=Q_ℓ(1), G=the unit gives infinite Frobenius image and F⊗G=F. Thus localement constant here is a terminology slip, not a failure of the tensor construction. The correct class is the same twisted-constant category as the hypotheses.

items.verdict: The equivariant splitting assertion is false, not just a missing proof; use the canonical torsion quotient instead.
items.french_reading: Printed p.269 asserts the equivariant representative F may be written uniquely F=P⊕T with P locally free and T torsion; p.270 repeats this for A-sheaves.
items.mathematical_context_and_resolution: Counterexample: let C_ℓ act continuously on M=Z_ℓ⊕F_ℓ by g(a,t)=(a,t+a mod ℓ). Then g^ℓ=1, the torsion submodule is T=0⊕F_ℓ, and M/T≅Z_ℓ has trivial action. An equivariant section would send 1 to (1,c), but g(1,c)=(1,c+1), contradiction. Thus a free complement need not be invariant, even for a finite group. On each connected component the quotient by torsion is a finite torsion-free Z_ℓ-module, hence free, and the quotient morphism becomes invertible in the rational coefficient category. For the intended finite extension L/Q_ℓ its integer ring A is a DVR (in particular Dedekind), and the same torsion-quotient repair applies. This gives the Hom bifunctor without claiming integral splitting. Classification is in the requested French-correction bucket, but the defect is a false mathematical assertion, not merely a typographical glyph.

items.verdict: Read within the finite coefficient-algebra context; explicitly translate as finite extension, recording the original wording.
items.french_reading: Printed p.270 says extension de type fini de Q_ℓ; preceding p.267 §1.4.3 restricts coefficient L to a finite Q_ℓ-algebra.
items.mathematical_context_and_resolution: The immediately preceding coefficient category has L a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-algebra, so a coefficient field here is a finite algebraic extension. The later EN9272 also explicitly says finite extension. In that intended context A is finite free over Z_ℓ, is a DVR, and A[1/ℓ]=L. If “finite type extension” were instead allowed to mean finitely generated as a field, take L=Q_ℓ(t). Its integral closure A is still Z_ℓ, so finite-freeness and the Dedekind property alone do NOT disprove the wording. The failure is A[1/ℓ]=Q_ℓ≠L: the asserted quotient category then gives Q_ℓ-sheaves, whose unit endomorphisms are Q_ℓ, rather than L-sheaves with unit endomorphisms L. Thus the original wording has an implicit finite-algebraic coefficient-field restriction which the Chinese should make explicit.
